title: SIP & Lumpsum Wealth Calculator
content:
# SIP & Lumpsum Wealth Calculator: The Complete Compounding Handbook Whether you are starting your very first **₹1,000 monthly Systematic Investment Plan (SIP)** from your first paycheck or planning to deploy a **₹10 Lakh one-time lumpsum bonus**, this institutional-grade compounding simulator calculates your future maturity corpus, accrued gains, and inflation-adjusted purchasing power with mathematical precision. {{CALCULATOR_WIDGET}} --- ## Part 1: Beginner's Blueprint — Understanding the Magic of Compounding ### 1.1 What is a Systematic Investment Plan (SIP)? In simple Indian words, an SIP is **not an investment product by itself**; it is a **disciplined method of investing**. Just like an automated Recurring Deposit (RD) cuts a fixed amount from your salary account on the 5th of every month, an SIP automatically deducts a pre-set amount and invests it into your chosen mutual fund scheme. > **💡 The "Chai-Sutta & Weekend Swiggy" Reality Check:** > Most young professionals in Mumbai, Bengaluru, Delhi, or Pune easily spend ₹150 to ₹250 a day on incidental treats — cutting chai, quick snacks, or weekend food deliveries. That is approximately **₹5,000 per month**. > * If you spend ₹5,000/month, at the end of 20 years you have **₹0**. > * If you channel that exact same **₹5,000/month into a disciplined equity SIP** averaging a realistic 12.5% annual return, your total investment of ₹12 Lakhs compounds into a massive **₹48.9 Lakhs**! ### 1.2 Simple Interest vs. Compound Interest: Why Time Beats Timing When you keep money in a traditional Fixed Deposit (FD) or Savings Account, you earn interest only on your original principal. But compounding is what Albert Einstein famously referred to as the **"Eighth Wonder of the World"** — you earn interest on your principal, and then you earn **interest on your accumulated interest**. Here is how compounding leaves simple savings behind over time with a ₹10,000 monthly investment: | Time Horizon | Total Invested | Bank FD @ 6.5% Simple Return | Mutual Fund SIP @ 12.5% CAGR | The Compounding Edge (Extra Wealth) | |---|---|---|---|---| | **5 Years** | ₹6,00,000 | ₹7,07,000 | ₹8,25,000 | **+₹1,18,000** | | **10 Years** | ₹12,00,000 | ₹16,98,000 | ₹23,23,000 | **+₹6,25,000** | | **15 Years** | ₹18,00,000 | ₹30,88,000 | ₹51,80,000 | **+₹20,92,000** | | **20 Years** | ₹24,00,000 | ₹50,38,000 | ₹1,00,90,000 (₹1.01 Cr) | **+₹50,52,000** | | **25 Years** | ₹30,00,000 | ₹77,73,000 | ₹1,90,00,000 (₹1.90 Cr) | **+₹1.12 Crore!** | *Takeaway:* Notice how by Year 25, while your total bank savings struggle under ₹78 Lakhs, your mutual fund SIP crosses **₹1.90 Crore**! Over 60% of that final corpus was generated in the last 7 years alone. ### 1.3 Rupee-Cost Averaging (RCA): Why Market Falls Are Actually a "Diwali Sale" The biggest psychological fear of every new investor is: *"What if the stock market crashes right after I invest?"* With an SIP, a market crash is actually your greatest financial advantage due to **Rupee-Cost Averaging**. When the market drops, mutual fund Net Asset Values (NAVs) fall, which means your fixed monthly installment buys **more mutual fund units**. When the market recovers and makes new all-time highs, those extra discounted units generate explosive returns. #### **A Simple 4-Month Math Example:** Imagine you invest ₹2,000 every month into an index fund: | Month | Market Condition | Fund NAV (₹) | Monthly SIP (₹) | Units Allotted | Cumulative Units Owned | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | **Month 1** | Normal Market | ₹50 | ₹2,000 | 40 units | 40 units | | **Month 2** | Panic Crash / Bear Dip | **₹25** | ₹2,000 | **80 units!** | 120 units | | **Month 3** | Market Recovery Rally | ₹40 | ₹2,000 | 50 units | 170 units | | **Month 4** | New Highs | ₹60 | ₹2,000 | 33.3 units | 203.3 units | | **Total** | — | **Avg NAV: ₹43.75** | **₹8,000** | — | **203.3 Units** | * **Your Total Capital Invested:** ₹8,000 * **Current Portfolio Value at Month 4:** 203.3 units × ₹60 NAV = **₹12,198** * **Net Profit:** **+₹4,198 (+52.5% Gain!)** * **Average Cost Per Unit:** ₹8,000 ÷ 203.3 = **₹39.35** (significantly cheaper than the simple average NAV of ₹43.75). *The Lesson:* You did not need to predict the exact bottom of the market crash. The automated nature of SIP forced you to accumulate maximum units at ₹25 without panic. --- ## Part 2: Intermediate Strategies — SIP vs. Lumpsum & Step-Up Compounding ### 2.1 SIP vs. Lumpsum: Which One Should You Choose? | Parameter | Systematic Investment Plan (SIP) | One-Time Lumpsum Investment | |---|---|---| | **Best Suited For** | Salaried employees with recurring monthly income | Windfalls (Diwali bonus, land sale, business payout) | | **Market Timing Risk** | **Zero timing risk** — spreads purchases across cycles | **High timing risk** — buying at peak can lead to short-term drawdown | | **Ideal Market Stance** | Consolidating, sideways, or volatile choppy markets | Deep post-crash valuations (e.g. March 2020 COVID trough) | | **Investor Psychology** | Stress-free automated habit; removes emotional FOMO | High anxiety; requires iron stomach to watch short-term red days | > **🔥 Pro-Tip: The Systematic Transfer Plan (STP) Workaround:** > If you have a lump sum of ₹10 Lakhs right now and the market is trading near historic highs, **never invest 100% into equity on day one**. > Instead, park the ₹10 Lakhs in a low-risk **Liquid or Ultra-Short Duration Fund** earning 6.5% to 7% annual interest, and initiate a weekly **Systematic Transfer Plan (STP)** of ₹25,000 to ₹50,000 into an Equity Flexicap or Nifty 50 Index Fund over 6 to 12 months. This gives you the peace of mind of an SIP with the earning power of a lump sum! ### 2.2 The 8-4-3 Rule of Wealth Creation Every seasoned Dalal Street investor understands that compounding acts like an exponential rocket: * **The First ₹1 Crore takes ~8 to 10 years:** During this phase, 75% of your portfolio consists of your own hard-earned deposited salary. Returns feel modest, and patience is tested. * **The Second ₹1 Crore takes only ~4 years:** Here, your accumulated gains equal your principal. Your money begins working harder than you do. * **The Third ₹1 Crore takes barely ~3 years:** By this stage, market gains dwarf your fresh monthly deposits. A simple 15% bull market year adds ₹45 Lakhs to your net worth in 12 months! ### 2.3 The "Rahul vs. Priya" Story: The Unstoppable Power of Step-Up SIP Most people's salaries increase by 8% to 15% every year due to appraisals and promotions. If your income grows, why should your investment remain stagnant? Let us compare two colleagues, **Rahul** and **Priya**, both starting their careers at age 25 with a ₹10,000/month SIP expecting 12% CAGR over 20 years: * **Rahul (Flat SIP):** Invests ₹10,000 every single month for 20 years without ever increasing it. - *Total Principal Invested:* ₹24,00,000 (₹24 Lakhs) - *Final Maturity Corpus:* **₹99,91,479 (~₹1.0 Crore)** * **Priya (10% Annual Step-Up SIP):** Starts with ₹10,000/month, but every year after her appraisal, she steps up her SIP by 10% (₹11,000 in Year 2, ₹12,100 in Year 3, etc.). - *Total Principal Invested:* ₹68,70,000 (₹68.7 Lakhs) - *Final Maturity Corpus:* **₹1,65,48,000 (~₹1.65 Crore)** *The Game Changer:* With a step-up increment that was barely felt in her monthly budget, Priya created **an extra ₹65.5 Lakhs of clean wealth**! --- ## Part 3: Advanced Portfolio Engineering & Institutional Insights ### 3.1 Direct Plan vs. Regular Plan: The 1% Leakage That Costs You ₹35 Lakhs When you buy mutual funds through your local bank relationship manager or third-party distributor, they place you into a **Regular Plan**. When you invest through platforms like Zerodha Coin, Groww, or direct AMC portals, you invest in a **Direct Plan**. Both plans own the **exact same shares of Reliance, TCS, HDFC Bank, and Infosys**, and are managed by the exact same fund manager. The only difference is the **Expense Ratio**: * **Regular Plan:** Charges ~1.75% to 2.25% annually (includes distributor trail commissions). * **Direct Plan:** Charges ~0.50% to 1.00% annually (zero distributor commissions). > **⚠️ The ₹35 Lakh Math Trap:** > A seemingly tiny difference of **1.0% in annual expense ratio** on a ₹20,000 monthly SIP over 25 years compounds into a staggering loss of **over ₹35,00,000 (₹35 Lakhs)** in distributor commissions! Always verify that your fund scheme name includes the word **"Direct - Growth"**. ### 3.2 XIRR vs. CAGR: Why CAGR Gives You False Numbers for SIPs * **CAGR (Compound Annual Growth Rate):** Assumes a single lump sum invested at the start and held continuously until the end. It only looks at the first deposit and the final value. * **XIRR (Extended Internal Rate of Return):** Calculates the exact annualized rate of return across multiple cash inflows occurring on different calendar dates. Because an SIP involves 120 separate investments over a 10-year period (where your 1st installment had 120 months to compound, but your 119th installment had only 1 month), **CAGR is mathematically meaningless for SIPs**. Always use **XIRR** to measure your actual mutual fund performance on your CAS (Consolidated Account Statement) or broker dashboard. ### 3.3 The Real Inflation Threat (6% Indian CPI Reality Check) Accumulating ₹1 Crore sounds like a dream, but what will ₹1 Crore actually buy when you retire 20 years from now? In India, long-term consumer price inflation (CPI) averages around **6% per year** (education and healthcare inflate at 8% to 10%). Using the rule of discounted purchasing power: $$\text{Real Purchasing Power} = \frac{\text{Nominal Corpus}}{(1 + 0.06)^{\text{Years}}}$$ * **₹1 Crore in 10 Years** has the purchasing power of only **₹55.8 Lakhs** today. * **₹1 Crore in 20 Years** has the purchasing power of only **₹31.1 Lakhs** today. * **₹1 Crore in 25 Years** has the purchasing power of only **₹23.3 Lakhs** today. *Rule for Goal Planning:* If your dream flat or child's overseas education costs ₹50 Lakhs today, do not aim for ₹50 Lakhs 15 years later. Target a future corpus of at least **₹1.20 Crore** using the calculator's inflation footnote. ### 3.4 Indian Mutual Fund Taxation Guide (Budget 2024 Updates) Understanding the tax implications on your mutual fund redemptions ensures you keep the lion's share of your wealth: #### **A. Equity Mutual Funds (≥65% Domestic Equities):** * **Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG):** - Applicable when units are held for **more than 12 months**. - **₹1.25 Lakh per financial year is 100% Tax-Free** (increased from ₹1.0 Lakh in Union Budget 2024). - Gains exceeding ₹1.25 Lakh are taxed at a flat rate of **12.5%** (without indexation). * **Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG):** - Applicable when units are redeemed within **12 months** of purchase. - Taxed at a flat rate of **20%** (increased from 15% in Budget 2024). #### **B. Debt Mutual Funds:** * Any redemption gains (short-term or long-term) are added directly to your total annual taxable income and taxed according to your individual income tax slab. > **💡 The Annual Tax-Harvesting Trick:** > Every February or March, savvy Indian investors sell equity mutual fund units with accrued gains up to **₹1.25 Lakhs** tax-free, and immediately reinvest that money back into the same or another fund. This resets their purchase cost base higher and saves lakhs in future capital gains tax! --- ## Part 4: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
1. What happens if I miss an SIP installment due to insufficient bank balance?

The Mutual Fund AMC will NEVER penalize you or cancel your portfolio. However, your bank may charge an NACH/ECS mandate bounce fee (typically ₹250 to ₹500 plus GST). If your bank balance is low, you can easily use your broker app to "Pause" your SIP for 1 to 3 months before the scheduled deduction date without any charge.

2. Is there a "Best Date" of the month to schedule my SIP (e.g. 1st, 5th, or 15th)?

No. Statistically, there is zero meaningful difference. Comprehensive backtesting of 20+ years of Nifty 50 data across the 1st, 7th, 15th, and 25th of every month revealed an annualized return difference of less than 0.08%. The best date is simply 2 to 3 days after your monthly salary is credited (e.g. 5th or 7th) to ensure your investment happens before discretionary expenses begin.

3. Can I withdraw my SIP money whenever I want? Is there any lock-in?

Except for ELSS (Tax Saving Mutual Funds) which have a mandatory 3-year statutory lock-in, all open-ended mutual funds (Flexicap, Largecap, Midcap, Index Funds) offer 100% liquidity. You can redeem your money anytime and the funds will credit to your verified bank account within T+1 to T+2 business days. Note that withdrawing within 365 days may attract a minor 1% Exit Load.

4. Is my money safe in mutual funds? Can the AMC or broker run away with my money?

Mutual funds in India are regulated by SEBI under a strict 3-tier governance structure: Sponsor → Trustee Board → Asset Management Company (AMC). Your securities are never held in the bank account of the AMC or your broker; they are held by independent, SEBI-licensed institutional custodians (such as Deutsche Bank, Citibank, or SBI Custodial Services). Even if an AMC or broker shuts down, your units remain safely registered with RTAs (CAMS or KFintech) under your PAN.

5. Should I stop my SIP during a market crash or recession?

Stopping your SIP during a crash is the single most costly mistake in investing. When stock prices collapse, your fixed monthly SIP buys maximum units at rock-bottom prices. When the market inevitably recovers, those discounted units generate the bulk of your multi-year compounding. Stopping your SIP during a downturn is like running away from a 40% discount festival at your favorite store!

6. What is the difference between SIP, Bank Recurring Deposit (RD), and PPF?

* Bank RD: Offers a guaranteed fixed interest rate (around 6.5% - 7.0%), but interest is fully taxable as per your income slab, resulting in post-tax returns that often fail to beat real inflation.
* Public Provident Fund (PPF): Offers EEE (Exempt-Exempt-Exempt) tax benefits at ~7.1% interest, but comes with a rigid 15-year lock-in and an annual deposit ceiling of ₹1.5 Lakh.
* Equity SIP: Carries market volatility in the short run, but historically delivers 12% to 15% CAGR over 10+ year horizons, generating 2x to 4x greater wealth than traditional debt instruments.

7. How many mutual fund SIPs should an investor run simultaneously?

Most retail investors over-diversify by holding 10 to 15 different mutual funds, creating massive portfolio overlap. For 95% of investors, 3 to 4 well-chosen funds are ideal:
• 1 Broad Market Index Fund (Nifty 50 or Nifty LargeMidcap 250)
• 1 Active Flexi-Cap or Multi-Cap Fund
• 1 Mid-Cap or Small-Cap Fund (for high-growth alpha)
• 1 Conservative/Emergency fund (Liquid or Arbitrage Fund)

8. What is the difference between "Growth" and "IDCW" (Dividend) options in SIP?

In the Growth option, all corporate profits, dividends, and capital gains are automatically reinvested back into the scheme, triggering full exponential compounding. In the IDCW (Income Distribution cum Capital Withdrawal) option, dividends are periodically credited to your bank account and taxed at your marginal income tax slab. For long-term wealth creation, always choose the Growth option.

9. How does taxation work when redeeming an SIP (FIFO Method)?

Redemptions in mutual fund SIPs follow the First-In, First-Out (FIFO) accounting method. Each monthly installment is treated as an independent investment with its own distinct holding period. When you withdraw money, the units bought in Month 1 are sold first. If those units were bought more than 12 months ago, their gains qualify for the lower 12.5% Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax rate.

10. Can I get a loan against my mutual fund SIP portfolio instead of selling?

Yes. It is called Loan Against Mutual Funds (LAMF). Leading banks and NBFCs allow you to digitally pledge your mutual fund units as collateral and offer an overdraft credit line up to 50% of your equity portfolio value at attractive interest rates (typically 9.5% to 10.5%). This lets you manage emergency cash requirements without selling your units, interrupting compounding, or triggering capital gains tax.

11. What is an Exit Load and when does it apply?

An Exit Load is a fee charged by the AMC if an investor redeems units before a pre-specified holding period. For most Indian equity funds, the exit load is 1% if redeemed within 365 days (1 year) of unit allotment, and 0% (Nil) after 1 year. The exit load is automatically deducted from your redemption NAV and credited back to the fund scheme.

12. What rate of return should I realistically assume in an Indian SIP Calculator?

Over historical 15 to 20-year horizons, India's benchmark Nifty 50 Total Returns Index (TRI) has compounded at approximately 12.5% to 13.5% CAGR, reflecting the underlying expansion of the Indian economy. For financial goal planning, conservative advisors suggest using 11% to 12% for Large-Cap/Index Funds and 13% to 14.5% for well-managed Flexicap or Midcap Funds.

# Fundamental Analysis Kaise Karein? Stocks Chunne Ka Tarika

Share market mein hazaaron companies listed hain, aur har beginner ke mann mein ek hi sawal hota hai: "Achha stock kaise chunein?" Iska sabse bharosemand jawab hai **fundamental analysis**. Is article mein hum samjhenge ki **fundamental analysis kaise karein**, kaun se ratios dekhne chahiye aur ek simple checklist ke saath kaise shuruaat karein.

## Fundamental Analysis Kya Hai?

**Fundamental analysis** ek aisa tarika hai jisme hum kisi company ki asli value (intrinsic value) ka andaza lagate hain. Isme company ke business, financial statements, management, industry aur future growth potential ko dekha jaata hai. Maqsad yeh pata karna hai ki share ka current market price us company ki value ke mukable sasta hai, mehnga hai ya fair hai.

Aise samjhein: agar aap ek dukaan kharid rahe hain, toh aap uski kamaai, location, karza aur future potential dekhte hain. Fundamental analysis share ke liye wahi kaam karta hai.

## Fundamental Analysis vs Technical Analysis

| Point | Fundamental Analysis | Technical Analysis |
|---|---|---|
| Focus | Company ka business aur financials | Price charts aur patterns |
| Time horizon | Long-term | Short-term |
| Kiske liye | Investors | Traders |
| Data | Balance sheet, P&L, cash flow | Price aur volume |

Beginners jo lambe samay ke liye invest karna chahte hain, unke liye fundamental analysis ek solid foundation hai.

## Fundamental Analysis Ke Main Components

### 1. Qualitative Analysis (Gunatmak)
Yeh woh cheezein hain jo numbers mein nahi aatin:

- **Business model:** Company paisa kaise kamati hai? Kya aap use samajh paate hain?
- **Management quality:** Promoters ka track record aur honesty.
- **Competitive advantage:** Strong brand, loyal customers ya low cost, jise "moat" kehte hain.
- **Industry outlook:** Kya sector badh raha hai ya sikud raha hai?

### 2. Quantitative Analysis (Sankhyatmak)
Yahan hum company ke financial statements ke numbers dekhte hain.

## Key Financial Statements

- **Profit & Loss Statement:** Revenue, expenses aur net profit dikhata hai.
- **Balance Sheet:** Company ki assets, liabilities aur equity ki position.
- **Cash Flow Statement:** Operations, investment aur financing se aane-jaane wala paisa.

Tip: Sirf profit nahi, **operating cash flow** bhi dekhein. Agar profit dikh raha hai lekin cash nahi aa raha, toh yeh red flag ho sakta hai.

## Important Ratios Jo Har Investor Ko Jaanne Chahiye

### 1. PE Ratio (Price to Earnings)
**Formula:** Share price / Earnings per share (EPS)

Yeh batata hai ki aap company ke ₹1 profit ke liye kitna paisa de rahe hain. High PE ka matlab ho sakta hai ki stock mehnga hai ya market ko growth ki ummeed hai. Hamesha PE ko usi sector ki doosri companies aur company ke apne past PE se compare karein.

### 2. EPS (Earnings Per Share)
**Formula:** Net profit / Total shares

Agar EPS saalon se badh raha hai, toh yeh company ki growth ka achha signal hai.

### 3. ROE (Return on Equity)
**Formula:** Net profit / Shareholders' equity x 100

ROE batata hai ki company shareholders ke paise par kitna return kama rahi hai. Lagataar achhe ROE (aam taur par 15% ya usse zyada) wali companies aksar quality business maani jaati hain.

### 4. ROCE (Return on Capital Employed)
Yeh dikhata hai ki company apni total capital se kitna efficiently kama rahi hai. Zyada ROCE achhi capital efficiency batata hai.

### 5. Debt to Equity Ratio
**Formula:** Total debt / Shareholders' equity

Kam debt wali companies mushkil samay mein zyada surakshit hoti hain. Aam taur par 1 se kam ratio comfortable maana jaata hai, lekin banks aur NBFC jaise sectors mein yeh alag hota hai.

### 6. Profit Margin
**Operating margin** aur **net margin** dekhein. Stable ya badhta margin achhi pricing power ka signal hai.

### 7. Dividend Yield
**Formula:** Annual dividend per share / Share price x 100

Yeh batata hai ki aapko share price ke mukable kitna dividend milta hai.

### 8. Price to Book Ratio (PB)
Share price aur company ki book value ka comparison, khaaskar banking aur financial sector ke liye useful.

## Fundamental Analysis Kaise Karein: Step-by-Step Process

1. **Sector chunein:** Aise sector se shuru karein jise aap thoda samajhte hain.
2. **Company ke baare mein padhein:** Annual report, investor presentation aur concall transcripts dekhein.
3. **Pichle 5 se 10 saal ka data check karein:** Revenue aur profit growth ka trend dekhein.
4. **Key ratios nikaalein:** PE, ROE, ROCE, debt-to-equity aur margins.
5. **Competitors se compare karein:** Same sector ki 3 se 4 companies ko side by side dekhein.
6. **Valuation check karein:** Kya price growth ke hisaab se reasonable hai?
7. **Risk factors dekhein:** Debt, regulation, competition, promoter pledging jaise points.
8. **Decision lein aur track karein:** Har quarter ke results dekhte rahein.

## Free Tools Jo Aapki Madad Karenge

- **Screener.in:** Financial data aur ratios ke liye popular screener.
- **NSE aur BSE websites:** Official filings aur announcements.
- **Company ki investor relations page:** Annual reports aur presentations.
- **Moneycontrol aur Tickertape:** Quick overview aur comparisons.

## Red Flags Jinse Bachna Chahiye

- Lagataar badhta hua debt
- Promoter ki shareholding mein tez girawat ya zyada pledging
- Profit ke saath cash flow ka na badhna
- Baar baar accounting ya auditor ke changes
- Bina clear business model ke hype wali company

## Fundamental Analysis Mein Common Galtiyan

- Sirf ek ratio dekhkar decision lena
- Sasta PE dekhkar kharidna (kabhi kabhi sasta hone ki wajah hoti hai)
- Sector ke difference ko ignore karna
- Sirf past data dekhna aur future ka outlook na dekhna
- Diversification na karna

## Fundamental Analysis Kaise Karein: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**1. Kya fundamental analysis ke liye commerce background zaroori hai?**
Nahi. Basic maths aur thoda practice kaafi hai. Concepts ko step-by-step seekha ja sakta hai.

**2. Kitne saal ka data dekhna chahiye?**
Kam se kam 5 saal, aur ho sake toh 10 saal ka data, taaki alag-alag business cycles ka asar samajh aaye.

**3. Kya fundamental analysis se hamesha profit hota hai?**
Nahi. Isse risk kam karne aur behtar decision lene mein madad milti hai, lekin market mein koi guarantee nahi hoti.

**4. Kya fundamental aur technical analysis dono saath use kar sakte hain?**
Haan, kai investors fundamental se stock chunte hain aur technical se entry timing dekhte hain.

**5. Sabse important ratio kaun sa hai?**
Koi ek ratio kaafi nahi hota. ROE, ROCE, debt aur growth jaise kai factors ko saath mein dekhna chahiye.

## Conclusion

**Fundamental analysis kaise karein**, ye seekhna ek achha investor banne ki taraf pehla bada kadam hai. Company ka business samjhein, financials ka trend dekhein, valuation check karein aur lambe samay ke liye soch rakhein. Jaldbaazi se bachein aur dhairya rakhein, kyunki achhi companies ko bhi wealth create karne mein time lagta hai.

> **Disclaimer:** Yeh article sirf educational purpose ke liye hai. Yeh kisi stock ko kharidne ya bechne ki salah nahi hai. Share market investments market risk ke adheen hain. Nirnay lene se pehle apni research karein ya SEBI-registered advisor
